overview: City-states are the small powers of the map: one city each, no victory of their own, and a bonus for whoever earns their loyalty. You earn it with envoys. One envoy opens the type bonus, three and six deepen it, and the player with the most envoys (at least three) is suzerain, gaining the city's unique bonus, its resources, and the right to levy its army for gold. A city-state can also be conquered, which ends its bonuses for everyone and angers the rest.
envoy_rules: Envoys come from civics (most civics in the first three eras grant one), from policy cards (Diplomatic League doubles the first envoy; Charismatic Leader and Gunboat Diplomacy add more), from completing a city-state's quest, from the Apadana and Kilwa Kisiwani wonders, from Amani the governor, and from alliance levels. Suzerainty needs the most envoys and at least three; a tie leaves the city without a suzerain. Envoys sent to a city-state at war with you are lost; envoys never expire otherwise. The AI competes hardest for Scientific and Industrial cities; Religious and Cultural ones are often cheap.

city_states.name: Anshan
city_states.suzerain_bonus: +2 Science from each Great Work of Writing; +1 Science from each Relic and Artifact.
city_states.real_world: An Elamite capital in the Zagros foothills of Iran, one of the oldest cities in the world.

city_states.name: Bologna
city_states.suzerain_bonus: Districts with a building provide +1 Great Person point of their type.
city_states.real_world: Home of the oldest continuously operating university in Europe, founded in 1088.

city_states.name: Fez
city_states.suzerain_bonus: Converting a city with a religious unit for the first time earns 20 Science per Population.
city_states.real_world: Morocco's medieval capital; its Qarawiyyin mosque-university dates to 859.

city_states.name: Geneva
city_states.suzerain_bonus: +15% Science in all cities whenever you are not at war with any civilization.
city_states.real_world: Calvin's republic on Lake Geneva, later the seat of the Red Cross and the League of Nations.

city_states.name: Hattusa
city_states.suzerain_bonus: Provides 2 of each Strategic resource per turn that you have revealed but not improved.
city_states.real_world: Capital of the Hittite empire in central Anatolia, abandoned around 1200 BCE.

city_states.name: Mitla
city_states.suzerain_bonus: City growth rate is 15% higher in cities with a Campus.
city_states.real_world: A Zapotec religious centre in Oaxaca, famous for its geometric stone mosaics.

city_states.name: Nalanda

city_states.real_world: A Buddhist monastic university in Bihar that taught for seven centuries until the twelfth.

city_states.name: Taruga
city_states.suzerain_bonus: +5% Science in all cities for each different improved Strategic resource they have.
city_states.real_world: An Iron Age site of the Nok culture in Nigeria, where iron was smelted by 500 BCE.

city_states.name: Antananarivo
city_states.suzerain_bonus: +2% Culture for each Great Person ever earned, up to 30%.
city_states.real_world: Capital of the Merina kingdom and of Madagascar, set on twelve hills.

city_states.name: Ayutthaya
city_states.suzerain_bonus: Gain Culture equal to 10% of the construction cost when finishing buildings.
city_states.real_world: The Siamese capital for four centuries, sacked by Burma in 1767.

city_states.name: Caguana

strategy: Spend the first three envoys on one city-state, not one each: suzerainty is the prize and three is the threshold.
A Scientific or Industrial city-state next to the AI will be contested; a Religious or Cultural one will usually be yours for six envoys all game.
Levy a city-state's army when a war is already won on paper and you need bodies, or when a militaristic neighbour is about to take the city-state itself.
Quests are free envoys. Check them every ten turns; most are things you were about to do.
A city-state that a rival conquers stops paying everyone. Gorgo, Pericles and Suleiman all want the Kumasi or Valletta on their border alive.
